decision_conditions:
3 YEAR CONSENT PERIOD: The development hereby permitted shall be begun not later than the expiration of three years from the date of this permission.

REASON: To comply with the provisions of Section 91(1)(a) of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 as amended by the Planning and Compulsory Purchase Act 2004 (Chapter 5).
description:
I am the leaseholder of the flat and I own all the windows in the flat under the Deed of Variation dated the 15th of June 2017, The Schedule, Clause 1.1. This includes window glass the internal and external surface materials of all the windows and the frames of all the windows. I own my doors under the lease dated 25th April 2000, Clause 3 (a)(6). This includes the doors and door frames.

The block of flats is owned by Islington Council. The block is located in the Whitehall Park Conservation Area, but it is not a listed building.

The block of flats has three storeys. My flat is located on the first floor. The windows and the balcony door referred to in this application are located on the rear elevation of the building.

During major works a few years ago, due to the age and poor condition of windows and balcony doors on the rear elevation of the building, the Council replaced single glazed timber windows and single glazed timber balcony doors at the rear of the building in all flats with modern double glazed UPVC windows and balcony doors, except for mine.  My windows and balcony door were not replaced, as they are my responsibility as leaseholder under the Deed of Variation.  They are old and in a very poor condition. I would like to replace them with modern double glazed UPVC windows and balcony door, which will also bring them in line with all the other windows and balcony doors on the rear elevation of the building.

The proposed works include replacing three single glazed timber windows and one single glazed timber balcony door in my flat, on the rear elevation of the building, with three double glazed UPVC 'A' Energy Rated windows and one double glazed UPVC 'B' Energy Rated balcony door, as described in a detailed specification attached to this application.

The replacement windows and the door are of an appropriate design and of similar quality to the ones that were installed by the Council at the rear of the building, and would not cause any adverse impact on the setting or significance of the building. They have a similar visual appearance in terms of their shape, colour and size/type of frame.

The proposed new windows and balcony door are of high quality and are A energy rated (windows) and B energy rated (door). They are thermally efficient and will eliminate heat loss within the flat as well as condensation, draughts, and noise.  As such, they will not only keep my home warm, but also help to reduce carbon emissions.

I will use a best-in-class windows installation provider, FENSA registered. The company is called ‘Barnet Window Company’, website link: www.barnetwindowcompany.co.uk. They are committed to playing their part in the fight against climate change by improving the thermal efficiency of the homes in our community. Their service also includes the removal and responsible disposal of old windows and doors. They work closely with their waste partners to make sure that they prioritise waste reduction, reuse, and recycling.
subdivision_of_building: Rear first floor. The proposal only affect my flat, located on the first floor.

phasing_details.phase_detail: Single Phase. The time schedule for the works will be determined after the planning permission is granted.
